s: Today's episode is a little different, because today is review day.
Instead, we are going to lock in the forty words you learned over the last four days.
Monday we went into the kitchen.
And yesterday, we talked about the internet.
Ten review words are the stars of today's show, and we will say each one at least three times, so they really stick.
Let's start with Sunday's career words.
What did we learn about an internship?
An internship is a short period of work experience, and it is often the first real step in a career.
My cousin did an internship at a newspaper, and that internship turned into her first job.
That's a great example, because an internship is exactly that, a door into a career.
Networking is meeting people who can help your career.
I got my current job through networking at a conference.
When you go networking, you are not just chatting.
You are building the relationships that shape a career.
Good networking opens doors that applications alone cannot.
Quick word before we continue with the career words.

A probation is a trial period at the start of a new job.
During probation, the company watches you closely.
My friend's probation lasted three months.
If you do well in probation, you keep the job.
A bonus is extra money paid to workers in addition to their salary.
A bonus can be a thank you for hard work.
When a team hits its goals, the company often pays a bonus to every worker.
To resign is to officially leave your job.
He decided to resign after ten years at the bank.
When you resign, you usually give notice, so the company has time to hire a replacement.
Speaking of hiring, that was another Sunday word.
Hiring is how companies find new people.
Good hiring keeps a team strong.
And let's not forget entrepreneur, career, layoff, and applicant.
A career is your working life.
A layoff is when a company lets workers go.
And an applicant is someone who applies for a job.
So Sunday's career story goes like this.
If you pass probation, you stay.
Hard work can earn you a bonus.
Some people even become an entrepreneur.
But sometimes there is a layoff, and then a worker may have to resign and build a new career.
One more round for our review stars before the break.
And only resign when you are truly ready for the next step.
If an applicant survives probation, earns a bonus, but then decides to resign, was the internship worth it?
The internship gave the experience, the networking built the contacts, the probation proved the skill, and the bonus rewarded the work.
Resigning just means the next career chapter.
And that is the point of review day.
These words connect into real stories.
An internship, good networking, a fair probation, an earned bonus.
Even resign can be a positive word when you choose it.
Chewy means food that needs a lot of chewing.
Those cookies were soft in the middle and slightly chewy.
I love food that is chewy.
Bagels are better when they are chewy.
If the bread is not chewy enough, something is wrong.
Marinate, braise, caramelize, whisk, drizzle, poach, julienne, and glaze.
To marinate is to soak food in sauce before cooking.
To braise is to cook slowly in liquid.
To caramelize is to brown sugar in food.
Drizzle means to pour a thin stream.
Poach is to cook gently in hot water.
Julienne is to cut into thin strips.
And to glaze is to coat with a shiny sauce.
Leftovers are food saved from a meal.
Good leftovers make the best lunch.
So the recipe goes like this.
Whisk the sauce, caramelize the onions, julienne the carrots, poach the eggs, drizzle the dressing, and glaze the top.
If anything is chewy in a bad way, save the rest as leftovers.
Pair the verbs with the food.
You marinate meat, you braise tough cuts, you caramelize onions, you whisk eggs, you drizzle oil, you poach salmon, you julienne carrots, and you glaze the cake.
And when it all stays a little chewy, you know it is homemade.

An accessory is a small item, like a scarf or a necklace, that completes an outfit.
A simple necklace is the perfect accessory for that dress.
One great accessory can change the whole look.
The right accessory ties everything together.
Now, wardrobe, tailor, vintage, outfit, runway, boutique, fabric, bespoke, and silhouette.
A wardrobe is your collection of clothes.
A tailor sews clothes to fit.
An outfit is a set of clothes.
The runway is where models walk.
A boutique is a small shop.
And a silhouette is the shape of clothes on a body.
A bespoke outfit from a boutique, sewn by a tailor from the finest fabric, with a clean silhouette, shown on the runway.
Maybe something vintage from my wardrobe.
What is your favorite fashion word from Tuesday?
A bespoke outfit feels like luxury.
But accessory is the useful one.
One accessory can rescue a boring outfit.
The right accessory does more than a whole new wardrobe.
Even a vintage dress looks fresh with a modern accessory.
Mute, spam, and influencer are our review stars, and there was also viral, screenshot, webinar, podcast, firewall, reboot, and hashtag.
Mute means to silence a microphone, speaker, or notifications.
Please mute your microphone in the meeting.
When the ads get loud, I mute the TV.
If a group chat gets noisy, mute it.
Spam is unwanted messages sent to many people at once.
I get so much spam in my inbox that I miss important emails.
Spam filters help, but some spam always gets through.
An influencer is a person with a large online audience.
The influencer recommended a new skincare brand.
A smart influencer builds trust, and a lazy influencer just sells ads.
Let me add one more round for each.
So mute the noisy chats, delete your spam, and follow an influencer who teaches you something.
The rest: viral means spreading fast online.
A screenshot is a photo of your screen.
A webinar is an online class.
A podcast, well, you are listening to one.
And a hashtag groups posts by topic.
I will describe, you name the word.
A person who moves opinions online.
And when a post spreads fast?
We have all ten internet words down.
Mute the spam, follow the right influencer, and never skip a good webinar.
Let's close with a rapid recap of our ten review stars.
Bonus, networking, mute, probation, resign, internship, spam, influencer, accessory, chewy.
Say them with us one more time.
That wraps up our review day.
Forty words, four days, one big victory for your memory.
Tonight, tell someone about your day and use five of these words.
Say bonus, networking, chewy, accessory, and mute out loud.
